profile.address: Avenida de la Industria, 15, 28108 Alcobendas, Madrid, Spain
profile.reading:
DC02 is the second data center building on DATA4's MAD01 campus in Alcobendas, on the northern edge of Madrid, Spain, at Avenida de la Industria 15. DATA4 is a French headquartered data center developer and operator, founded in 2006 and based in Paris, led by chief executive Olivier Micheli since November 2014. The company designs, builds, finances, and operates its own facilities rather than developing for third party landlords, and its Madrid MAD01 campus is positioned toward colocation customers, cloud providers, and carriers, distinct from the newer, more hyperscale oriented MAD02 campus the company is separately building at San Agustín del Guadalix north of the city.

DC02 followed the campus's original building, DC01, into service in 2022 according to operator material reviewed for this campus, adding roughly 3,000 square meters of white space two years after DC01 opened in 2020, though this session did not independently reconfirm that exact commissioning date beyond the operator's own materials. A 2023 trade press account of DC03 breaking ground, sourced to the operator, put DC02 at 6.6 megawatts of IT capacity across 3,000 square meters, about 32,292 square feet, of white space, the same figure independently attributed to DC03. That same account described DC01, the campus's original and largest building, at 14 megawatts of IT capacity across 6,500 square meters, and described the finished MAD01 campus, at full build out, as an eight hectare site hosting six buildings totaling 70 megawatts. DATA4's own current Madrid landing page, by contrast, describes MAD01 as a single 50 megawatt campus across 4 hectares, a smaller figure that likely reflects capacity commissioned to date rather than the six building design end state described in 2023. This registry records both figures with attribution rather than resolving the gap between them.

DATA4's corporate ownership has changed twice since DC02 opened. AXA Investment Managers Alternatives sold DATA4 to Brookfield Infrastructure in a deal worth 2.4 billion dollars, agreed in April 2023 and completed that August. Then, in August 2025, Brookfield brought in Arjun Infrastructure Partners and Interogo Holding as new shareholders in a stake sale covering DATA4's stabilised hyperscale portfolio in Paris, Milan, and Madrid, a combined 244 megawatts of contracted capacity that a Brookfield SEC filing valued at 3.6 billion dollars. Brookfield kept a stake alongside the new investors, and DATA4's own management team, still led by Micheli, continues to run the business day to day. Because the August 2025 release names Madrid generally rather than MAD01 specifically, it is not possible to say from that document alone whether DC02 sits inside the divested stabilised pool or remains a separate, more recently commissioned asset.

No tenant name for DC02 was found in any operator or trade source reviewed. No standby generator rating, utility interconnection figure, or onsite generation figure specific to this building was found either, only the campus level IT capacity figure of 6.6 megawatts already described above, which this registry attributes to DC02 specifically because the 2023 trade press account named it as an IT capacity figure for that building by name, distinguishing it from the campus wide totals that mix marketing and design figures.

profile.campus_power_note: The four power numbers for DATA4's MAD01 campus need to stay separate because two different totals are in circulation. DATA4's own current Madrid page states the MAD01 campus is 50 megawatts across 4 hectares. A 2023 trade press account of DC03's groundbreaking, sourced to the operator, instead describes an eight hectare site designed for six buildings totaling 70 megawatts once fully built, with DC01 at 14 MW IT capacity, DC02 at 6.6 MW IT capacity, and DC03 at 6.6 MW IT capacity confirmed individually. Both totals describe IT capacity, not utility interconnection ratings, standby generator ratings, or onsite generation figures, none of which were found published for this campus. This registry treats the 50 MW / 4 ha figure as the operator's current simplified marketing number and the 70 MW / six building / 8 ha figure as the more detailed design end state, and records both here rather than picking one.
